title: Safe Management and De-escalation
subtitle: For staff at Pennsylvania personal care homes and assisted living facilities. 55 Pa. Code 2600.65(f)(6) and 2800.65(i)(6).

title: Seeing it coming, while it is still cheap to fix

eyebrow: Minutes before anyone raises a voice
title: What escalation looks like early
points: Pacing, or starting and abandoning things
The same question, over and over
Following you, or blocking a doorway
Hands: wringing, fists, picking at clothes
A voice that got faster before it got louder

title: Why reasoning stops working, and what replaces it

quote: Almost everything that looks like will not is actually cannot.
attribution: A resident who cannot follow three steps is not refusing them. Treat a cannot as a will not and you get a fight; treat a will not as a cannot and you lose nothing.

eyebrow: A reaction out of all proportion
title: What overwhelms a person with dementia
points: More than one instruction at a time
Being asked to remember something
Noise, mirrors, crowds, a running television
Late afternoon, when the day has used them up
Being touched before being spoken to

title: The thirty seconds before you start the task

eyebrow: How you walk in decides most of it
title: Entering a room without starting something
points: Knock, and wait to be seen before you move
Approach from the front, never the blind side
Say who you are and what you came to do
Get to eye level — standing over is pressure
Ask before you touch, every single time

eyebrow: The most reliable fix in this course
attribution: Not the whole plan for the next ten minutes. The next single step, and then enough silence for it to land. Most refusals are somebody who could not keep up saying so the only way they can.

title: What to actually say, out loud, in the moment
Sentences that lower the temperature
points: “You’re right, that isn’t fair.”
“I can hear how upset you are.”
“Tell me what happened.”
“We can do this later.”
“What would help right now?”

eyebrow: Every one of these adds pressure
title: Sentences that make it worse
points: “Calm down.”
“You have to let me do this.”
“I already told you.”
“Your daughter isn’t coming, she died.”
“There’s nothing to be upset about.”

title: The tasks this goes wrong in, almost every time
The care moments that start fights
points: Showers and bathing, by a wide margin
Dressing, and being undressed in front of someone
Toileting and incontinence care
Being moved — transfers, or leaving a room
Medication a resident does not want

eyebrow: Why the shower is the worst one
quote: You are asking someone to be undressed, cold, and held by a person they may not recognize.
attribution: Ask that of anybody and you would get a fight. Warm the room first, keep them covered, narrate every step before it happens, and let them hold something.

title: The line that does not move
The person in the room this course has not mentioned
When you are the one escalating
points: Your voice got louder and you did not decide to
You are explaining the same thing again, harder
You have started arguing about the facts
You want to win more than you want to leave
You are thinking about what they said last week

eyebrow: There is no medal for staying
quote: Handing a resident to a coworker is a skill, not a failure.
attribution: A resident who says no to you at nine and yes to somebody else at nine fifteen has told you nothing about your competence. Trade the task and take the next one.

eyebrow: Write what a camera would have seen
title: What goes in the note
points: What was happening right before it started
What they said, in their words
What you tried, and in what order
What they did — actions, not adjectives
How it ended, and who you told

eyebrow: What to carry out of this course
quote: You are not there to win the next ten minutes. You are there to get through them with nobody hurt.
attribution: That is a lower bar than winning, and it is the one that actually protects everybody in the room, including you.
